summary: The first of two assembly and test plants that CG Semi, the outsourced assembly and test venture of CG Power with Renesas and Stars Microelectronics, is building in Sanand, Gujarat. The Union Cabinet approved the INR 7,600 crore unit in February 2024 and its foundation stone was laid in March 2024. G1 was inaugurated on 28 August 2025 as a pilot-scale plant offering assembly, packaging and test of packages such as QFN, SOIC, BGA and flip-chip FCQFN and FCBGA, and it started commercial production on 4 July 2026. Its peak capacity is given as up to 300 million units a year.

CG Semi's releases on the G1 inauguration and the start of commercial production put spending at more than INR 7,600 crore over five years for G1 and G2 together, where the Cabinet approval had given INR 7,600 crore as the estimated cost.

milestones.note: Union Cabinet approval of the unit that covers both CG Semi facilities.

notes: CG Semi names a second facility, G2, about 3 km away, recorded separately as osat-cg-semi-sanand-g2. The investment and jobs figures cover both facilities. The CG Semi newsroom shows 17 August 2026 on the release about the G1 inauguration, but a news agency report of the same text is dated 28 August 2025, matching the July 2026 release; the newsroom copy is therefore recorded without a publication date.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Set the company to the parent CG Power, dated the G1 inauguration to 28 August 2025 with a news agency report, added the March 2024 foundation stone for the Sanand unit, and rewrote the summary, which named package families the sources do not list. Audit fixes (2026-11-07): kept both INR 7,600 crore figures because they are different statements, an estimated cost at Cabinet approval in 2024 and more than that amount over five years in CG Semi's later releases, and explained the change in their notes.
